text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, the continuation after A20 flipped to a different group of activities. A20 occurs once in every trace in both windows; in the earlier window about 82 in 100 of its outgoing transitions led to A24, A25 or A26 and only about 18 in 100 to A21, A22 or A23, while in the later window about 79 in 100 lead to A21, A22 or A23 and only about 21 in 100 to A24, A25 or A26 [DIR020, POS002].
- Participation swapped accordingly: A21, A22 and A23 each appear in about 79 in 100 traces in the later window (158 of 200) versus about 19 in 100 before (37–38 of 200), while A24, A25 and A26 each fall from about 82 in 100 (163–164 of 200) to about 21 in 100 (42 of 200) [OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024, OCC025].
- The two groups act as mutually exclusive alternatives: a member of A21–A23 and a member of A24–A26 shared a trace in at most about 1 in 100 cases earlier and in none later, and each group's three activities run together whenever the group runs (co-occurrence about 79 in 100 for A21–A23 later, about 82 in 100 for A24–A26 earlier). Within each group both orders occur in similar proportions, so neither window shows a fixed internal order [REL020, REL022, REL029, REL041, REL028].
- The swap happens at the same stage of the trace: mean relative event positions stay around 0.66–0.70 for all six activities in both windows, so the later block occupies the mid-trace position the earlier block had; what changed is how often the block runs [POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008].
- A10 appears in fewer traces and earlier: about 7 in 100 traces in the later window (14 of 200) versus about 17 in 100 before (33 of 200), with its median event position moving from about 0.86 to about 0.36; its outgoing transitions, previously almost always to A33 (about 97 in 100), are now spread across several targets [OCC010, POS001, DIR010].
- A32 and A33 each appear in about 10 more traces in 100 (about 60 to about 70 in 100); they now typically share traces with A21–A23 (co-occurrence with A21 about 9 to 56 in 100) rather than with A24–A26 (about 52 down to 15 in 100) [OCC030, OCC031, REL026, REL044].
- A15 and A16 repeat more often per trace: mean occurrences rise from about 1.69 to about 1.88 and 1.87 respectively, with full participation in both windows; A30 rises from about 1.63 to 1.75 [OCC015, OCC016, OCC028].
- The rare activities A02, A04, A06 and A08 appear somewhat more often (from about 1–2 in 100 traces to about 6–9 in 100) with visibly changed successor profiles, but these rest on only 2–4 traces earlier and 12–18 later, so the proportions are weak [OCC002, OCC004, OCC006, OCC008, DIR002, DIR004, DIR006, DIR008].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the alternative continuation after A20 reversed: in the earlier window traces typically continued with the block A24–A25–A26 (about 82 in 100 cases), whereas in the later window they typically continue with the block A21–A22–A23 (about 79 in 100 cases), with the previously dominant block now taken in only about 21 in 100 cases. The flip is shown directly in A20's outgoing-transition profile, based on all 200 traces in each window and larger than in about 99 of 100 random re-splits, and it is consistently mirrored by the occurrence counts (37–38 versus 158 of 200 traces; 163–164 versus 42), by the relation, position and lag indicators, and by both blocks keeping the same mid-trace position [DIR020, OCC020, OCC023, REL011, REL014, POS003, POS006].

Limitations: the many relation and lag items restate the same flip and are not independent confirmations; the evidence shows the two blocks as alternatives but cannot show whether they are one-for-one substitutes in the underlying flow; and it cannot rule out that the two windows simply capture a different mix of case types rather than a modified flow [REL020, REL041, DIR020, OCC020, OCC023].

Other differences:
- A10's lower participation, earlier event positions and spread of outgoing transitions are not explained by the routing flip and may be a separate difference; its support is modest (33 versus 14 traces) [OCC010, POS001, DIR010].
- A15, A16 and A30 now repeat more often per trace [OCC015, OCC016, OCC028].
- A32 and A33 occur in about 10 more traces in 100 and now co-occur with A21–A23 rather than A24–A26; this is consistent with being downstream of the rerouted block, but no direct successor change into A32/A33 is observed [OCC030, OCC031, REL026, REL044].
- A02, A04, A06 and A08 occur somewhat more often with changed successors, on very few observations [OCC002, OCC004, OCC006, OCC008, DIR002, DIR004, DIR006, DIR008].
